purpose: Review records for the Sukkah foundations block.

primaryText.hebrew: סוכה שהיא גבוהה למעלה מעשרים אמה פסולה ורבי יהודה מכשיר

translation.text: A sukkah higher than twenty cubits is unfit; Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner reading physical structure and validity claims.
encounters.learningObjective: Map a physical condition, validity ruling, and dissent before asking for a reason.

languageSupport.grammarNote: Hold the structure, threshold, ruling, and dissent apart.

encounters.context: The opening Mishnah states a validity rule. The learning encounter explains source reasoning, not practical construction guidance.

assessment.bestAnswer: Name the structure, height condition, validity ruling, and Rabbi Yehuda's dissent.
assessment.rationale: The learner sees the case before comparing reasons.
misconceptions: Treating the number as detached from the structure.
assessment.transferPrompt: In a new source, name structure, condition, ruling, and dissent.

encounters.safetyBoundary: Text study only; consult a qualified halakhic authority for personal practice.

review.secondSourceContext: Eruvin 2a shares the height threshold but asks a different question.
review.retrievalTrigger: Weekly review or a missed source-map item.

primaryText.hebrew: למען ידעו דורותיכם · וסוכה תהיה לצל יומם · בסוכות תשבו
primaryText.editorialNormalization: Short source cues for a guided comparison.

translation.text: For generations to know · a sukkah for daytime shade · dwell in sukkot.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner ready to distinguish several rationales for one ruling.
encounters.learningObjective: Compare purpose-based explanations without flattening them into one claim.

glosses: למען ידעו — so that generations know
languageSupport.grammarNote: Each cited verse is used to articulate a different explanatory path.

encounters.context: Rabba, Rabbi Zeira, and Rava each offer a reason connected to a different scriptural source. The block teaches comparative argument reading.

assessment.bestAnswer: State the distinct function each rationale gives the height rule.
assessment.rationale: Different sources can support different accounts of one condition.
assessment.transferPrompt: When several reasons appear, name what each makes central.

encounters.safetyBoundary: Text study only; no practical ruling is implied.

review.secondSourceContext: Eruvin 2a provides a parallel height discussion for comparison.
review.retrievalTrigger: Return after a missed purpose-or-source item.
